subject: science
passage: In parts of Africa, a small bird called the greater honeyguide helps people find honey. Honey hunters in Mozambique, for example, make a special trilling call as they walk through the bush. A honeyguide that hears the call often answers and then flies ahead, leading the hunters to a bees' nest hidden in a tree. After the people open the nest and take the honey, the bird feeds on the leftover beeswax.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Honey hunters in Mozambique have learned to imitate the songs of many birds.
choices.B: Honeyguides and human honey hunters work together in a way that helps both.
choices.C: Greater honeyguides feed mainly on the honey they find in bees' nests.
choices.D: Honeyguides answer calls made by people in nearly every part of the world.

explanation.why: The bird leads the hunters to a bees' nest, and the people open the nest, take the honey, and leave beeswax that the bird eats. The text as a whole describes this partnership, in which each side gains something.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The hunters make one special call; the text never says they imitate many birds.
explanation.B: Correct. The people get honey, and the bird gets the beeswax, so the cooperation helps both.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the people take the honey and the bird eats the leftover beeswax.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes this behavior only "in parts of Africa," so this claims far too much.
